tldr: LLaMP is a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation framework using hierarchical ReAct agents to interact with the Materials Project database and run atomistic simulations, enabling accurate, hallucination-resistant retrieval and generation of materials science knowledge without fine-tuning.
contributions: Introduction of a multimodal RAG framework employing hierarchical ReAct agents that dynamically interact with the Materials Project database.
Proposal of a statistical metric (Self-consistency of Response) to assess the reproducibility and usability of LLM responses in high-precision scientific settings.
Evaluation of LLaMP against vanilla LLMs on predicting bulk moduli, electronic bandgaps, formation energies, and magnetic orderings.
Demonstration of real-world applications in inorganic synthesis recipe extraction and crystal structure generation/editing.
Integration of high-throughput atomistic simulation workflows with pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potentials.
methods: The authors developed LLaMP, a hierarchical orchestration system where a supervisor ReAct agent delegates queries to specialized assistant agents that interact with the Materials Project API and other tools. They defined a Self-consistency of Response (SCoR) metric combining precision and confidence to evaluate response reproducibility. The framework was benchmarked on material property prediction tasks (bulk modulus, bandgap, formation energy, magnetism) and real-world applications such as crystal structure editing and annealing molecular dynamics simulations using pre-trained ML force fields.
results: LLaMP reduces the mean absolute error for bulk modulus prediction from ~40 GPa (vanilla LLMs) to 14.57 GPa. For bandgap retrieval, LLaMP achieves a Self-consistency of Response (SCoR) of 0.938. In magnetic ordering classification, LLaMP with GPT-4 backend achieves 0.98 accuracy and an R² of 0.992 for magnetization prediction. Vanilla LLMs exhibit large variances (MAE 1.5–5.5 eV) for formation energies and hallucinate elastic tensor components (e.g., predicting C₁₁ = 289.2 GPa for NaCl instead of the DFT value of 76 GPa).
limitations: Vanilla LLMs suffer from hallucination, low-fidelity knowledge retrieval, and inability to handle higher-order data such as tensors and 3D crystal structures without external grounding. Fine-tuning approaches lack scalability and long-term memory retention. Flat planning strategies fail due to excessive cognitive load and schema‑parsing errors. GPT-3.5‑based LLaMP struggles to distinguish total magnetization from magnetization per formula unit and cannot differentiate ferromagnetic from ferrimagnetic orderings.
